svg.title: On postoperative day 2 after a sleeve gastrectomy, a client has a heart rate of 128/min with mild abdominal pain and a temperature of 100.2 F. Which action should the nurse take first?
svg.desc: Unexplained tachycardia after bariatric surgery is an anastomotic leak until proven otherwise and is a surgical emergency, so the provider is notified at once for a CT scan. Incisional pain, low-grade fever, and decreased bowel sounds alone are expected — it is the tachycardia that changes this picture.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Anastomotic Leak
Read the situation
On postoperative day 2 after a sleeve
gastrectomy, a client has a heart rate of
128/min with mild abdominal pain and a
temperature of 100.2 F. Which action
should the nurse take first?
What fits here
Notify the provider immediately about the
unexplained tachycardia
Why it fits
Unexplained tachycardia after bariatric
surgery is an anastomotic leak until
proven otherwise and is a surgical
emergency, so the provider is notified at
once for a CT scan. Incisional pain, low-
grade fever, and decreased bowel sounds
alone are expected — it is the tachycardia
that changes this picture.
